name: Coinbase BTC/USD multi-level taker sweep
description: Within one ingested Coinbase BTC/USD trade batch sharing one event timestamp, aggressive flow on one side that consumes at or above min_levels (K) distinct prices is a sweep. detection_state is sweep when a side qualifies and quiet otherwise; a batch spanning exactly K-1 distinct prices does not fire. On detection the signal emits swept_levels (distinct prices consumed), swept_size (total consumed base size on that side), and direction (buy or sell). This is a state-shaped signal with a latest-sweep payload and a quiet default: the adopted spot set has no emit-only-on-detection signal to mirror, so a non-sweeping batch publishes detection_state = quiet and leaves the retained latest sweep unchanged. Every state-dependent field is always present: before any sweep has fired there is nothing retained, so the payload is the explicit sentinel direction = none with swept_levels 0 and swept_size 0 rather than a missing field. When both sides qualify in one batch the deeper level count wins, then the larger swept size, then buy, so the choice is deterministic. min_levels defaults to 3. This identity is single-venue by construction: the measurement compares one venue's own trades and book against each other, so it reads only Coinbase inputs and is ready whenever the Coinbase book-and-trade join is fresh, independently of the other adopted spot venue. No blended `btc.external.*` variant of this measurement is published: a cross-venue form would have to rule which venue's book prices another venue's trade, and that ruling is deferred pending evidence (ADR 0023 amendment and ADR 0024, both 2026-09-02). Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
